title: Lvalue references
recap: An lvalue reference is an alias bound to an existing object. Reading or assigning through it accesses that object rather than an independent reference-owned value.
A non-const lvalue reference must bind to an appropriate modifiable lvalue. It cannot be reseated to a different object after initialization.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement addTo(target,delta). target is an int lvalue reference: change the caller's integer by adding delta. delta may be negative or zero. Inputs and sums fit int. A reference is an alias to the existing object, not a separate copy to return.
hints: Negative delta is a valid addition.
